comparison: Perfect agreement on Mafb expression pattern (C25-C33). Both accept the temporal and spatial expression data from immunostaining and Western blot as convincing evidence for Mafb's developmental expression pattern.

Perfect agreement on functional auditory defects (C60-C66). Both accept the ABR and DPOAE data demonstrating that synaptic defects cause abnormal auditory responses while hair cell function remains intact.

Strong agreement on postsynaptic defects (C47-C57). Both accept the immunofluorescence, electron microscopy, and quantification showing reduced GluR2 puncta and PSD size as convincing evidence, though peer reviewers request additional mRNA analysis.

Agreement on specificity of Mafb effects (C67-C70, C121-C122). Both accept electrophysiological data showing normal intrinsic neuronal properties, supporting that Mafb specifically affects synaptic differentiation without altering general neuronal maturation.

Agreement on Gata3-Mafb genetic relationship (C84-C89, C5-C6, C91-C94). Both accept the epistasis experiments and rescue data as convincing evidence that Mafb acts downstream of Gata3 in postsynaptic differentiation.

Partial agreement on gain-of-function effects (C71-C79). Both accept the data showing transient increases in postsynaptic markers and normal final synapse numbers, but peer reviewers question whether effects are due to precocious expression versus overexpression.

Disagreement on interpretation of precocious Mafb expression (C72-C73, C76, C123). OpenEval supports the conclusion that precocious expression accelerates development, while peer reviewers are 'not entirely convinced,' suggesting effects could be due to overexpression rather than timing.

Disagreement on sufficiency of mechanistic evidence (C58-C59). OpenEval considers the in situ data showing no mRNA changes as supporting a post-transcriptional mechanism, while peer reviewers explicitly request this experiment, indicating they view the mechanism as uncertain and requiring investigation.

Agreement on early SGN development and specificity controls (C39-C45 overlap with C40-C41, C43-C44). Both accept that early development proceeds normally and that various control experiments support the specificity of Mafb's role.
Agreement on conditional allele validation (C39, C42 overlap with C34-C35). Both accept the genetic tools and their validation, enabling functional studies of Mafb.
Agreement on conditional allele generation (C34-C38 overlap with C34-C35, C39, C42). Both accept the molecular validation and phenotypic characterization of the conditional allele.
Agreement on electrophysiological controls (C121-C122). Both accept that early Mafb overexpression does not adversely affect SGN maturation, supporting specificity of Mafb's synaptic effects.
Agreement on Gata3-Mafb expression relationship (C80-C83). Both accept the immunostaining data showing co-expression, loss of Mafb in Gata3 mutants, and restoration by MafbCE.

Major disagreement on main conclusions (C1-C3, C90-C92 vs C1-C2, C90, C95, C104, C108). OpenEval supports the terminal selector interpretation, while peer reviewers explicitly challenge this, noting that vestibular neurons form ribbon synapses without Mafb and that overexpression doesn't create ectopic synapses.

Partial agreement on genetic hierarchy (C4-C6, C93-C94). Both accept the Gata3→Mafb relationship and necessity/sufficiency data, though peer reviewers question the broader terminal selector interpretation.

Disagreement on sufficiency interpretation (C4, C123). OpenEval supports sufficiency claims based on gain-of-function data, while peer reviewers question whether transient effects on GluR2 clustering demonstrate true sufficiency.

Major disagreement on terminal selector model (C95, C102-C105, C104). OpenEval supports Mafb as a terminal selector based on established criteria, while peer reviewers explicitly reject this interpretation, proposing alternative mechanisms involving synaptogenic adhesion molecules.
Agreement on specificity controls (C46, C54, C59). Both accept that normal targeting and efferent innervation support the specificity of postsynaptic defects.
Agreement on control experiments (C59). Both accept normal efferent innervation as supporting the specificity of the SGN postsynaptic phenotype.
Agreement on genetic relationship (C91-C92). Both accept that Mafb acts downstream of Gata3 in the genetic hierarchy controlling postsynaptic differentiation.
OpenEval identifies literature context claims (C7-C23, C96-C100, C106-C107, C109-C113, C118) as properly cited background knowledge. Peer reviewers do not separately evaluate these contextual claims.
OpenEval rates microarray data claim (C24) as uncertain due to incomplete presentation. Peer reviewers do not specifically address this preliminary observation.

Partial overlap on speculative claims (C101, C108, C114-C115, C117, C119). OpenEval rates these as uncertain/speculative. Peer reviewers challenge C108 (therapeutic implications) as part of their broader critique of the terminal selector interpretation.
OpenEval evaluates factual observations (C116, C120) about adult expression and model limitations. Peer reviewers do not separately address these observational claims.
